title: Local quasi-finite projection with bounded relative dimension
statement: Let $B$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $g:Y\to B$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] of $Y$, and let $N\ge0$ be an integer such that every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $g$ has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. Then there are an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq Y$ of the image point of $y$, an integer $d$ with $0\le d\le N$, and a morphism $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_B$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] which is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and quasi-finite (of finite type with finite discrete fibres, [pqf-def-quasifinite]), whose composite with the projection $\mathbf A^d_B\to B$ is $g|_U$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version: first reduction by a quasi-finite projection; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $B=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Since $g$ is locally of finite type and $B$ is affine, choose an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of the image point of $y$ such that $g(U)\subseteq B$ and the induced ring map $R\to A$ is of finite type. This is exactly the affine-pair characterization of locally finite type.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01T2, affine-pair characterization of locally finite type

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the fibre of $h=g|_U:\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ over $\mathfrak p$ has underlying space $U\cap g^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$, an open subspace $W$ of the underlying space $g^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$ of the fibre of $g$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_n$ is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $W$, their closures $\overline{Z_i}$ in $g^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$ are irreducible and closed, and $\overline{Z_i}\cap W=Z_i$, so they form a chain of the same length in $g^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$. Hence the fibre of $h$ has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. The morphism $h$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: it is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], because for affine opens $U'\subseteq U$ and $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ with $h(U')\subseteq V$, $U'$ is an affine open of $Y$ with $g(U')\subseteq V$, so $\mathcal O(V)\to\mathcal O(U')$ is of finite type by the same lemma applied to $g$; and it is quasi-compact because a morphism of affine schemes is affine [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and affine morphisms are quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Apply [lem-trf-weak-relative-noether-normalization] to $h$ to obtain an integer $d$ with $0\le d\le N$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to A$ whose induced morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_d])$ is quasi-finite.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0GTG, together with the definition of fibre dimension and the open-subspace chain inclusion

proof.text: The homomorphism defines an $R$-morphism $e:U\to\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_d])=\mathbf A^d_B$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space]; since it is an $R$-algebra homomorphism, $R\to R[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to A$ is the structure map $R\to A$, so the composite of $e$ with the projection to $B$ is $g|_U$. As $U$ and $\mathbf A^d_B$ are affine, $e$ is affine [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. By Step 2, $e$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]: of finite type, and every point of $U$ is isolated in its fibre. Each fibre $U\times_{\mathbf A^d_B}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(q)=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{R[T]}\kappa(q))$ is affine, so its underlying space is quasi-compact; a quasi-compact space all of whose points are isolated is finite and discrete. So $e$ has finite discrete fibres.

I split its proof into the affine chart supplied by local finite type, the weak relative Noether normalization theorem (new child node lem-trf-weak-relative-noether-normalization), and the translation of the polynomial-ring map to a separated quasi-finite morphism to relative affine space. The fibre bound is preserved on the open affine chart because irreducible chains in an open fibre are chains in the original fibre. I searched the whole DAG and blueprint for Tag 0GTG and for relative quasi-finite projections; no duplicate exists. The local source PDF named by the import is unavailable, so the proof follows the local Stacks formulation of Tag 0GTG and records the source need below. Maintainer reader (2026-10-18): Step 2 now takes closures for the chain comparison and derives that $h$ is a finite-type morphism (the child's hypothesis) from the affine-pair lemma and the affine-morphism nodes; Step 3 cites the affine-schemes node for affineness of $e$ and derives finite discrete fibres from isolated points plus quasi-compactness of the affine fibres.
